name: Cleveland Public Power
takeaway: City of Cleveland operates Cleveland Public Power alongside FirstEnergy (Illuminating Co). Address determines which utility serves the account. CPP addresses are exempt; FirstEnergy/Illuminating Co addresses ARE eligible for competitive supply and NOPEC aggregation.
hook: Do you know if your electric comes through Cleveland Public Power or through FirstEnergy? Sometimes we see both on the same street.
notes: Major gotcha for Cuyahoga County calls. Cleveland city limits contain both CPP and Illuminating Company service territories. CPP is a city-owned municipal utility — completely exempt from retail choice. Illuminating Company accounts within Cleveland are eligible for competitive supply. Always verify by address. Do not assume every Cleveland address is CPP.

name: Columbus Division of Power
utility: Columbus Division of Power / AEP Ohio
takeaway: City of Columbus operates its own Division of Power in certain neighborhoods alongside AEP Ohio. Address determines which utility serves the account. CDP addresses are exempt; AEP addresses ARE eligible and may qualify for Clean Energy Columbus aggregation.
hook: Do you know if your electric is through AEP or through Columbus Division of Power? It varies by neighborhood.
notes: Columbus Division of Power (CDP) serves portions of Columbus in competition with AEP Ohio. CDP accounts are municipal and exempt from retail electric choice. AEP Ohio accounts in Columbus ARE eligible and participate in the Clean Energy Columbus aggregation (10.01¢ → moving terms). Always verify service address before assuming aggregation eligibility.
